data.title: Unattended Workstations Left Unlocked
data.summary: Workstations were left logged in and unlocked in unoccupied areas, giving anyone with physical access an authenticated session with the user's full access to mail, files and internal applications.
data.description:
An unlocked workstation is the shortest path from the lobby to the network, requiring no exploitation at all. Within a short absence an attacker can read and send mail as the user, copy data, insert a persistence mechanism, or run a payload that establishes remote access.

Everything done is attributed to the legitimate user, by every log that records it, which makes later investigation misleading as well as difficult.

The behaviour is a consequence of friction: long passwords, frequent timeouts and slow unlocks teach people to avoid locking. Reducing that friction changes the behaviour more reliably than instruction does.
data.recommendation:
* Enforce a screen lock after a short idle period by policy, and apply it to meeting-room and shared machines too.
* Reduce the cost of locking and unlocking — proximity or biometric unlock, and badge-out triggered locking.
* Disable USB mass storage and human-interface-device injection where the role does not require it, to limit what a brief access achieves.
* Include an unlocked-workstation sweep in routine security walks, leaving a note rather than a sanction.
data.short_recommendation: Enforce short screen locks and make locking automatic.
